title: The One-Minute Habit
passage:
Mika wanted to improve her English speaking, but she did not enjoy practicing long speeches. She often stopped because she worried about making mistakes. One day, her teacher suggested a different method: speak for only one minute about something nearby. At first, Mika thought the task was too easy. The teacher told her to choose any object, such as a pencil case, a plant, or a school bag, and explain what she noticed. The goal was not to use difficult words. The goal was to keep speaking, even when she had to change her sentence. Mika began with her water bottle. She described its color, where she bought it, and why she carried it every day. She made several grammar mistakes, but she finished the full minute. The next day, she spoke about the view from her classroom window. After a week, she noticed that she was pausing less. Then Mika added a new rule. After speaking, she wrote down one word or expression that she had wanted to use but did not know. She looked it up later and tried to use it the next day. This made her practice more useful because the new words came from things she actually wanted to say. A month later, her class had a short discussion activity. In the past, Mika had usually waited for other students to speak first. This time, she raised her hand. Her answer was not perfect, but she was able to explain her idea without becoming silent. Mika understood that her improvement had not come from one long practice session. It had come from many short attempts that felt safe enough to repeat. She still wanted to study grammar and learn more vocabulary, but she no longer believed she had to be fully prepared before speaking. Her one-minute habit also changed her attitude toward mistakes. A mistake was no longer proof that she could not speak English. It was information about what to practice next. Soon, two friends joined her, and they took turns choosing daily topics. Sometimes they laughed at unusual sentences, but they corrected each other kindly and continued. The small routine gave Mika something more valuable than perfect sentences: confidence built through repetition and the feeling that speaking was a skill she could train a little every day.

Mika also began recording herself once a week. She did not listen for every mistake. She listened for longer pauses, unclear ideas, and expressions she wanted to improve. Comparing recordings from different weeks helped her notice progress that was difficult to feel from one day to the next.
translation:
美香は英語を話す力を伸ばしたいと思っていましたが、長いスピーチ練習は苦手でした。間違いを気にして途中で止まってしまうからです。そこで先生は、身近なものについて一分だけ話す方法を勧めました。難しい単語を使うことではなく、言い直しながらでも話し続けることが目標です。美香はまず水筒について、色、買った場所、毎日持ち歩く理由を話しました。文法の間違いはありましたが、一分間話し切ることができました。翌日は教室の窓から見える景色について話し、一週間後には止まる回数が減っていることに気づきます。さらに、話したあと『言いたかったけれど知らなかった表現』を一つ書き留め、後で調べて翌日に使うというルールを加えました。自分が本当に言いたかった内容から新しい表現を学べるため、練習がより実用的になりました。一か月後のクラス討論では、以前なら他の人が話すのを待っていた美香が自分から手を挙げました。完璧ではなくても、黙り込まず考えを説明できました。上達は一度の長時間練習ではなく、繰り返せる小さな挑戦から生まれたのだと気づきます。間違いも『自分は話せない証拠』ではなく、『次に練習すべきことを教える情報』だと考えられるようになりました。やがて友人二人も加わり、毎日テーマを交代で決めました。おかしな文に笑うことがあっても、互いにやさしく直しながら続けました。この一分習慣が美香に与えたのは、完璧な英文よりも、反復から生まれる自信と、話す力は毎日少しずつ鍛えられるという実感でした。

美香は週に一度、自分の声も録音するようになりました。すべての間違いを探すのではなく、長い間、分かりにくい説明、次に改善したい表現に注目しました。数週間分の録音を比べると、一日ごとでは気づきにくい上達も確認できました。
